selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed skiing abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski school lessons for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking 8-hour panoramic journey through frozen valleys, towering viaducts, and snow-capped peaks. Family-friendly with panoramic windows, dining car service featuring Swiss fondue and raclette, and commentary in multiple languages. A magical winter experience for all ages.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais & Graubünden

experiences.name: Family Tobogganing on Faulhorn-Bussalp Run
experiences.description: Experience one of the longest natural toboggan runs in the Alps, stretching over 15km from Faulhorn down to Grindelwald. Rent sleds at the top and race down through snowy forests and open meadows. This thrilling yet safe activity is a highlight for families and requires no prior experience. Warm up afterward with hot chocolate at a mountain hut.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Gather around a traditional Swiss fondue pot in a cozy chalet restaurant in Verbier. Dip crusty bread into melted Gruyère and Emmental cheese blends, paired with local white wine or apple juice for kids. Many restaurants also offer raclette, where cheese is melted tableside over potatoes and pickles. A quintessential cultural dining experience that families love.

experiences.name: Ice Skating at Davos World's Largest Natural Ice Rink
experiences.description: Lace up your skates at the Davos natural ice rink, one of the largest in the world at over 18,000 square meters. Open to all skill levels with skate rentals available on-site, this iconic winter activity is perfect for families looking for a fun break from skiing. The rink is surrounded by mountain scenery and has a warming hut serving Swiss hot chocolate and Bratwurst.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Focus on transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Geneva airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked budget train or shared shuttle transfer to the Swiss Alps resort area (SBB Swiss Federal Railways offers affordable night connections). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport before or after landing — try a Migros or Coop grab-and-go sandwich (CHF 5–8). Many Swiss train stations also have budget kiosks open late.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your train tickets via SBB.ch for best prices. Swiss Half Fare Card (CHF 120) is worth purchasing if you plan multiple train trips during the week. Keep arrival energy low — big ski days start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely morning settling in. Head to the hotel breakfast if included, then gear up for your first alpine adventure. Visit the local ski rental shop early to secure budget equipment rentals — booking in advance online (e.g., Ski-hire.com or Intersport) can save 20–30% vs. on-site rentals. Get fitted for skis, boots, and helmets for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hit the beginner and intermediate slopes at the nearest ski resort to the hotel. Many Swiss resorts offer family ski areas with dedicated gentle runs perfect for all skill levels. Purchase a half-day afternoon lift pass to save money on your first ski day. Ski patrol and resort staff can guide first-timers on the best family-friendly runs.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski gear to the rental shop and head back to the hotel to warm up. Explore the resort village on foot — browse local shops and get oriented with the area. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local mountain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or pick up bread, cheese, and fruit from a Coop or Migros supermarket (CHF 8–12 per person) — a great budget strategy for the whole week.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from the supermarket to eat on the mountain (sandwiches, hot chocolate in a thermos). Avoids expensive on-mountain restaurant prices (CHF 25–40/person).
meals.dinner: Try a local Beizli (Swiss pub-style restaurant) in the village. Look for daily specials (Tagesmenü) which often include soup, main, and dessert for CHF 18–25. Try Rösti (Swiss potato dish) or Wurstsalat.

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental tip: Rent for the full week upfront — weekly rates are significantly cheaper than daily rates. Helmets are strongly recommended for children and available at all rental shops. Check if your hotel offers any ski pass partnerships or discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing! Start early to beat the crowds and enjoy freshly groomed morning pistes. Focus on improving technique — many resorts offer group ski lessons which are much more affordable than private instruction (CHF 40–60/person for a half-day group lesson vs. CHF 150+ for private). Enroll kids in ski school for a fun, supervised morning session.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore different runs and chairlifts. Take a scenic gondola or cable car to higher elevation viewpoints even if you don't ski every run — the panoramic Alpine views are spectacular and worth the experience. Look for blue (intermediate) runs for a confidence-building afternoon session.
day_by_day.evening: Ice Skating at Davos World's Largest Natural Ice Rink — Lace up your skates at the famous Davos natural ice rink, one of the largest in the world at over 18,000 sq meters. This is a fantastic family activity and a wonderful way to wind down after skiing. Skate rental is available on-site at reasonable prices (CHF 7–10 for skate hire). The evening atmosphere under the lights is magical.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered supermarket breakfast at the hotel room or apartment — yogurt, muesli, fruit, and Swiss bread (CHF 5–8/person).
meals.lunch: On-mountain self-service cafeteria — choose carefully and opt for soup and bread (CHF 10–15) rather than full meals. Alternatively, bring packed lunch from the supermarket.
meals.dinner: Fondue night! Find a budget-friendly fondue restaurant in the village. Cheese fondue is Switzerland's iconic dish and many casual spots offer it for CHF 20–28/person. It's hearty, warming, and perfect after a day on the slopes.

day_by_day.notes: Davos ice rink is open daily during winter season. Check opening hours and session times at the rink before heading over in the evening. Dress warmly in layers for ice skating — it can be significantly colder at the rink level. Group ski lessons should be booked the evening before or early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a rest day from skiing to let muscles recover and explore other winter sports. Try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) — trails are typically free or very low cost (trail pass CHF 5–10) compared to downhill lift passes. Cross-country skiing is excellent for families and a wonderful way to experience the quieter, forested Alpine landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing adventure! Rent snowshoes from a local outdoor shop (CHF 10–15/day) and explore marked snowshoe trails around the resort area. Many trails are free to use and offer stunning mountain scenery. This is a budget-friendly activity perfect for all ages, including younger children. Look for guided snowshoe tours which often include hot drinks for around CHF 25–35/person.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the village for some après-ski culture without the expensive drinks. Explore local Swiss craft shops, pick up affordable Swiss chocolate from a supermarket (Lindt, Cailler, or Frey brands are excellent value), and enjoy a warm Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate at a village café. Many villages have free evening events or live music in winter season.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or self-catered breakfast. Try making Swiss Birchermüesli — oats soaked overnight with apple and milk, a traditional Swiss breakfast staple (very affordable).
meals.lunch: Visit a local Bäckerei (bakery) for fresh bread rolls, pastries, and soup — a filling and budget-friendly lunch for CHF 8–12/person.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel room or apartment kitchen if available — pasta with a Swiss cheese sauce is easy, cheap, and warming. Alternatively, try a local döner kebab or pizza restaurant in the village for CHF 12–18/person.

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important for preventing ski fatigue and injury, especially for children. Snowshoeing requires no prior experience and is suitable for children aged 5+. Check local tourist office for free or low-cost activities — many Swiss resort villages offer free guided walks, cultural events, and family activities during winter season.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the slopes for another full ski day with renewed energy. By now the family should have improved confidence on skis. Try some new runs or explore a different sector of the mountain. Take the first gondola up to catch the sunrise over the Alps — a truly breathtaking experience that costs nothing extra with your lift pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try tobogganing (sledding) — one of Switzerland's most beloved and budget-friendly winter activities! Many resorts have dedicated toboggan runs (Schlittelbahn) which are either free or very low cost (CHF 5–10 for sled rental). Some runs are several kilometers long and offer an exhilarating family adventure. Check if your resort has a night toboggan run for an extra special experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel and enjoy a family movie night or board games. Many Swiss resort hotels have communal lounges with games and cozy fireplaces. This is a great budget evening that lets everyone recharge before the final ski days.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket self-catered breakfast. Stock up on provisions for the day including packed lunch supplies.
meals.lunch: Packed mountain picnic — Swiss cheese (Gruyère or Emmental), bread, dried fruit, nuts, and chocolate. Eat at a sunny mountain terrace or picnic area with panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Try a Raclette restaurant — another Swiss classic where melted cheese is scraped over potatoes, pickles, and cold meats. Many casual restaurants offer raclette for CHF 20–28/person and it's an interactive, fun family dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Toboggan runs are often busiest on weekends — Friday afternoon is a great time to visit before the weekend crowds arrive. Some toboggan runs require purchasing a separate ticket; check the resort website. Always wear a helmet when tobogganing. Night toboggan runs (if available) typically operate on specific evenings — check locally.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day — make the most of your lift pass! Head to any unchecked runs or sectors of the mountain. Consider taking a ski lesson to consolidate the week's learning. Many instructors offer end-of-week assessment sessions. Take family photos on the mountain to capture the memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a morning of skiing, try ice climbing or a winter via ferrata if available at your resort — a unique and exciting winter sport experience. Alternatively, visit the resort's winter fun park which often features snow tubing, mini ski jumps, and snowboard areas — great for kids and usually included in the lift pass or available for a small additional fee.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the final evening with a special budget-friendly dinner out. Many restaurants offer Saturday evening specials. Explore the village one last time, buy Swiss souvenirs from the Migros or Coop (Swiss chocolate, cheese, and fondue sets make affordable gifts), and enjoy a final Glühwein by an outdoor fire pit if available.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — treat yourselves to the full spread if available to fuel the final ski day.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch — allow a slightly larger budget for the final ski day. Try a traditional Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni with cheese, cream, and bacon) at a mountain hut restaurant (CHF 18–22).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell dinner — find a mid-range Swiss restaurant offering a set menu (Tagesmenü) for CHF 28–38/person. Try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal in cream sauce with Rösti) or a hearty Swiss mountain stew.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday slopes can be busier with weekend visitors — head out early to beat the crowds. Begin packing non-essential items in the evening to make Sunday morning departure smoother. Return ski rental equipment on Saturday evening if departing early Sunday to avoid extra rental day charges.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final hotel breakfast before departure. Take a scenic morning walk around the resort village to soak in the last Alpine views. Visit the local weekly market if available — Swiss mountain markets often feature local produce, cheeses, and handmade crafts at very reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, consider a brief stop in Zurich or Geneva for sightseeing. Zurich's Old Town (Altstadt) is walkable and free to explore — see the Grossmünster cathedral, Bahnhofstrasse, and Lake Zurich. Geneva's Jet d'Eau fountain and Old Town are equally impressive. Both cities are easily accessible by SBB train from major Alpine resort areas.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the departure airport for your return flight. Allow extra time for check-in, security, and potential winter weather delays. Grab a final Swiss treat — a Luxemburgerli macaron from Sprüngli at Zurich airport or a Swiss chocolate bar from the duty-free shop as a last taste of Switzerland.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy the Swiss spread one last time.
meals.lunch: Train station or airport Coop/Migros for affordable sandwiches, salads, and drinks (CHF 8–15/person). Much more budget-friendly than airport restaurants.
meals.dinner: Airport dining if needed before your flight — look for Coop restaurant or self-service options which are more affordable than sit-down airport restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours travel time from most Swiss Alpine resorts to Zurich or Geneva airports, plus check-in time. Swiss trains are extremely punctual and reliable. Keep all ski rental return receipts and lift pass receipts for any potential insurance claims. Swiss Alpine trips in February can involve flight delays due to weather — consider travel insurance. Total estimated budget per person for 7 days (excluding flights and accommodation): CHF 400–600, covering lift passes, equipment rental, food, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in Swiss Alps. Check-in and settle into your Beachfront-style alpine room.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at resort by approximately 23:30–00:00. Light welcome snack or room service to unwind after the journey. Review ski rental and activity options available at the resort front desk or concierge.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the departure airport before boarding.
meals.lunch: On the flight or at a transit airport restaurant.
meals.dinner: Room service or a light snack from the resort's late-night menu upon arrival. Budget approximately CHF 20–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Given the very late arrival at 22:30, no sightseeing or activities are planned for Day 1. Prioritize rest to be energized for the full alpine adventure ahead. Confirm ski equipment rental and lift pass bookings with the concierge first thing in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. After breakfast, visit the resort concierge to arrange ski equipment rentals, lift passes, and ski school bookings if needed. Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort village to acclimatize to the alpine altitude and get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for your first ski session of the trip. Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. Beginners and children can enroll in a group ski lesson (approximately CHF 65–85 per person for a half-day group lesson), while more experienced skiers can explore the groomed blue and red runs. Rent equipment at the slope-side rental shop if not done at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:00. Freshen up and head out for the Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Dinner Experience at a cozy local chalet restaurant nearby. Dip crusty bread into bubbling melted cheese and enjoy traditional raclette alongside local charcuterie, cornichons, and Swiss wine or hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or approximately CHF 18–25 per person. Fuel up with eggs, muesli, fresh bread, and Swiss cheese.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — try a classic Rösti with a fried egg or a hearty soup. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Dinner at a local chalet restaurant. Budget CHF 40–60 per person including a glass of Swiss wine or non-alcoholic drink.

day_by_day.notes: Altitude acclimatization is important on Day 2 — stay hydrated and apply high-SPF sunscreen, as alpine UV levels are intense even in winter. Book ski lessons in advance for children to secure spots in family-friendly group classes.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the resort, then head out for a full morning of skiing on the Jungfrau Region Slopes. With Day 2's warm-up behind you, tackle more challenging red or black runs if your skill level allows. Families can enjoy the dedicated beginner areas in Grindelwald with gentle wide slopes perfect for kids. Take advantage of the crisp morning snow conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mountain lunch break, transition from skiing to the legendary Family Tobogganing on the Faulhorn-Bussalp Run — one of the longest natural toboggan runs in the Alps at over 15km. Rent a toboggan at the top station and enjoy a thrilling, scenic descent through pristine alpine landscapes. This is a highlight activity for families and suitable for children aged 6 and up.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Relax in the resort's wellness facilities (sauna or hot tub if available) to soothe tired muscles. Enjoy a casual dinner at the resort's main restaurant or a nearby mid-range alpine bistro.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — CHF 18–25 per person. Load up on carbohydrates for an active day.
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain cafeteria on the Jungfrau slopes — soup, sandwiches, or a warm pasta dish. Budget CHF 18–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a local alpine bistro — try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal in cream sauce with Rösti) or a hearty alpine stew. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Toboggan rental is approximately CHF 10–15 per sled. The Faulhorn-Bussalp run requires a gondola or bus to reach the top — factor in approximately 30–45 minutes of travel time. Wear waterproof outerwear as tobogganing can be wet and snowy. Helmets are recommended for children.

day_by_day.morning: A rest-and-explore morning. Sleep in slightly, enjoy a relaxed breakfast, then take a scenic walk or snowshoe through the alpine village. Browse local shops for Swiss souvenirs — Swiss Army knives, chocolate, and handcrafted wooden ornaments make excellent gifts. Visit a local bakery for a mid-morning coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the legendary Glacier Express scenic train from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking panoramic journey through the Swiss Alps. The 8-hour full journey is iconic, but families can opt for a partial segment (e.g., Zermatt to Andermatt or Chur) for a 2–4 hour scenic experience that fits an afternoon slot. Enjoy panoramic windows showcasing glaciers, gorges, and snow-dusted valleys.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by train or transfer. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range Swiss restaurant in the village — try traditional Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) or a cheese-based alpine dish. End the evening with a warm Swiss hot chocolate or Glühwein (mulled wine) at a resort bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast or a local café — croissants, Swiss cheese, cold cuts, and fresh coffee. CHF 15–25 per person.
meals.lunch: Dining car on the Glacier Express — a unique Swiss railway dining experience. A set lunch menu costs approximately CHF 35–50 per person (reservation recommended).
meals.dinner: Village restaurant — traditional Swiss cuisine. Budget CHF 35–55 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express requires advance seat reservations, especially in peak February ski season. A scenic partial segment ticket costs approximately CHF 50–120 per person depending on the route chosen. Check the SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) website for timetables and book at least 2–3 days in advance. The panoramic windows are best enjoyed from the right-hand side of the train heading from Zermatt toward St. Moritz.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for your most ambitious ski day yet. With three days of experience, push your skills further — explore the higher altitude runs above Grindelwald or take a guided ski tour of the Mürren area for stunning Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peak views. Families with younger children can revisit favorite beginner runs and practice techniques learned in lessons.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a slope-side lunch, make your way to Davos for an afternoon of Ice Skating at the Davos World's Largest Natural Ice Rink — spanning over 18,000 square meters. Rent skates on-site and glide across the vast natural ice surface surrounded by alpine scenery. This is a wonderful family-friendly activity that provides a fun change of pace from skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Davos village briefly before heading back to the resort. Stop at a local fondue or raclette spot in Davos for dinner, or return to the resort area and dine at a nearby mid-range restaurant. Try a Swiss-style burger or a hearty Wurst platter at a casual alpine eatery.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — CHF 18–25 per person. Energize for a full active day.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — Rösti, soup, or a warm sandwich. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Casual mid-range restaurant in Davos or near the resort — try Bratwurst with onion gravy and Rösti or a Swiss-style pizza. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ice skate rental at Davos rink costs approximately CHF 8–12 per person. Entry to the rink is approximately CHF 6–10 per adult and CHF 4–6 per child. Travel time between Jungfrau area and Davos is approximately 1.5–2 hours — plan accordingly and depart the slopes by 13:30 to arrive comfortably for an afternoon session. Davos is best reached by train via the Rhaetian Railway.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated family ski day on the Jungfrau Region Slopes. This is your last full ski day — make the most of it! Explore any runs you haven't yet tried. More advanced skiers in the family can attempt the famous 'Inferno' area above Mürren while beginners continue to build confidence on gentler slopes. Consider a family ski photo session with a mountain photographer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a final mountain lunch, enjoy a relaxed afternoon of Family Tobogganing on the Faulhorn-Bussalp Run for a second time — now that you know the route, the whole family can race down with confidence and fully enjoy the 15km descent. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the resort's leisure facilities — swimming pool, sauna, or a gentle snowshoe walk near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant in the resort village. Choose a restaurant with panoramic mountain views if possible. Order a multi-course Swiss meal — start with a Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), enjoy a main of Fondue Bourguignonne (meat fondue), and finish with a Swiss chocolate dessert. Toast to a wonderful alpine adventure.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — CHF 18–25 per person.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the slopes — your final mountain meal. Treat yourselves to a slightly more indulgent lunch: try a Cordon Bleu or a raclette plate. Budget CHF 28–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a quality mid-range chalet restaurant — CHF 50–75 per person including a Swiss dessert and drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the busiest day on the slopes as weekend visitors arrive. Head out early (lifts open around 08:30) to beat the crowds on popular runs. Book your farewell dinner reservation in advance, as quality restaurants in Swiss alpine villages fill up quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort. Enjoy a relaxed last breakfast and take a gentle stroll through the alpine village to soak in the mountain atmosphere one last time. Browse any remaining souvenir shops — stock up on Lindt or Läderach Swiss chocolates, cheese, and local jams to bring home. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final light activity — a scenic cable car ride for panoramic alpine views, or a short snowshoe walk near the resort. If time is tight, head directly to the airport or train station for your departure transfer. Allow ample travel time as Swiss alpine routes can involve multiple transfers.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Travel to the airport for your return flight. Reflect on an incredible 7-day Swiss Alps adventure filled with world-class skiing, scenic train journeys, tobogganing, ice skating, and authentic Swiss culinary experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final resort buffet breakfast — CHF 18–25 per person. Enjoy a slow, indulgent last meal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a village café or airport restaurant before departure — try a Birchermüesli, a fresh sandwich, or a Swiss pretzel with cheese. Budget CHF 15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: At the airport or on the return flight.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at most Swiss alpine resorts is 11:00–12:00. Store luggage with the concierge if you plan any final morning activities. Swiss airports (Zurich, Geneva, Basel) are well-connected by train from alpine regions — allow 2–3 hours minimum for transfer plus check-in time. Don't forget to pick up Swiss chocolate at the airport duty-free as a last-minute treat!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Gather around a traditional Swiss fondue pot in a cozy chalet restaurant in Verbier. Dip crusty bread into melted Gruyère and Emmental cheese blends, paired with local white wine or apple juice for kids. Many restaurants also offer raclette, where cheese is melted tableside over potatoes and pickles. A quintessential cultural dining experience that families love.

experiences.name: Ice Skating at Davos World's Largest Natural Ice Rink
experiences.description: Lace up your skates at the Davos natural ice rink, one of the largest in the world at over 18,000 square meters. Open to all skill levels with skate rentals available on-site, this iconic winter activity is perfect for families looking for a fun break from skiing. The rink is surrounded by mountain scenery and has a warming hut serving Swiss hot chocolate and Bratwurst.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps. Check-in to your Beachfront suite and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night welcome amenity arranged by the resort: a bottle of Swiss Chasselas white wine, artisan cheese board, and warm fondue broth waiting in your suite. Light in-room dining recommended after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the departure airport.
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the departure airport.
meals.dinner: In-room private dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated late-arrival platter with Swiss charcuterie, Gruyère, Emmental, warm bread, and a selection of herbal teas and hot chocolate.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival at 22:30 means no sightseeing or activities on Day 1. Arrange a pre-booked private chauffeur transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in luggage storage with the resort concierge. Request a wake-up call and breakfast time for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort to recover from jet lag. At 10:00, meet your dedicated resort ski concierge for a full equipment fitting session — premium ski boots, skis, helmets, and heated gloves provided. Begin your first ski experience with a private ski instructor on the Jungfrau Region Slopes, exploring the interconnected runs of Grindelwald. Suitable for all skill levels within the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau slopes after a mountain-top lunch. Explore the intermediate and advanced runs above Grindelwald with your private guide. Take the Eiger Express gondola for panoramic views of the Eiger North Face. Return to the resort by 16:30 for a warm-down.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a family après-ski session at the resort's heated outdoor infinity pool and spa. Enjoy Swiss Alpine wellness treatments — hot stone massage and steam sauna available. Dress for dinner at 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss Alpine breakfast buffet at the resort's main restaurant — fresh pastries, bircher muesli, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and hot chocolate.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Grindelwald-First — a premium mountain restaurant with panoramic Eiger views. Try the Rösti with alpine herbs, veal sausage, and mulled wine.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Dinner Experience at a cozy chalet restaurant in the Verbier/Grindelwald area. Traditional cheese fondue, raclette, air-dried beef (Bündnerfleisch), and a curated Swiss wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private ski instructor at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Ensure all family members have appropriate ski insurance. The Jungfrau ski region requires a Top Ski Pass — the resort concierge can arrange multi-day passes. Weather permitting, visibility on the Eiger Express is spectacular in the afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart at 09:00 for the legendary Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride. Board the panoramic train from Zermatt to St. Moritz for an 8-hour breathtaking journey through 291 bridges, 91 tunnels, and the iconic Oberalp Pass. Reserve a premium first-class Excellence Class compartment with dedicated butler service, gourmet meal service on board, and floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the afternoon, passing through the Rhine Gorge (the 'Swiss Grand Canyon'), the Goms Valley, and the dramatic Furka Pass landscape. Enjoy the on-board gourmet lunch service with regional Swiss specialties and premium wine pairing as the scenery unfolds.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in St. Moritz in the early evening. Enjoy a private guided evening stroll through the iconic St. Moritz village, exploring the luxury boutiques on Via Serlas. Return to the resort by private transfer. Dinner at the hotel's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Express breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh croissants, fruit, yogurt, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board lunch on the Glacier Express Excellence Class — three-course menu featuring Swiss veal medallion, alpine herb risotto, and a chocolate fondant dessert with Valais wine pairing.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant — five-course tasting menu with Swiss-French fusion cuisine, featuring dishes like lake trout with beurre blanc, venison with juniper jus, and a Swiss chocolate soufflé. Pair with a sommelier-selected Swiss Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express Excellence Class must be booked well in advance (ideally 2–3 months ahead). Arrange a private luxury transfer to Zermatt station in the morning and a return transfer from St. Moritz in the evening. This is a full-day excursion — pack a small daypack with essentials, snacks, and a camera. The train offers some of the most iconic photography opportunities in Switzerland.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — optional yoga or pilates session at the resort's private wellness studio at 08:30. At 10:30, depart for the Family Tobogganing on the Faulhorn-Bussalp Run — one of the longest natural toboggan runs in the Alps at over 15km. Take the gondola up to Faulhorn peak for stunning 360-degree views before beginning the exhilarating descent. Toboggans are provided in premium quality; private guides accompany the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the toboggan run and enjoy a warm-up break at a mountain hut mid-run. Continue the descent to Bussalp at a leisurely pace, stopping for photos at scenic viewpoints. Return to the resort by 15:30. Enjoy the resort's heated pool and family relaxation area.
day_by_day.evening: Family movie night or board game evening in the resort's private lounge, available for exclusive booking. Followed by a relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked Alpine trout, freshly squeezed juices, and Swiss pastries.
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Berghaus Bussalp mountain hut — hearty alpine cuisine including Käseschnitte (Swiss cheese toast), pea soup, and hot apple cider for the family.
meals.dinner: Casual luxury dinner at the resort's brasserie — fondue bourguignonne (meat fondue), seasonal salads, truffle fries, and warm chocolate fondue with fresh fruits for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The Faulhorn-Bussalp toboggan run is suitable for children aged 6 and above. Ensure all family members wear helmets (provided). The run takes approximately 2–3 hours at a leisurely family pace. Check weather and run conditions with the resort concierge the evening before. Waterproof, warm layering is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a full day of premium skiing. Today, focus on the Wengen and Mürren sectors — car-free Alpine villages accessible only by train and cable car, offering a more serene and exclusive skiing experience. Private ski guide leads the family through off-piste powder runs (weather and conditions permitting) and the famous Lauberhorn race course.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, the adults can enjoy advanced runs on the Schilthorn (famous for the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service') while younger family members participate in a supervised ski school session at Mürren Ski School with certified instructors. Regroup at 16:00 and take the cable car to Piz Gloria revolving restaurant for hot chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 18:00. Enjoy a private family spa session — heated outdoor jacuzzi under the stars, sauna, and steam room. Dinner reservation at 20:30.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — emphasis on high-energy foods: granola, smoked meats, poached eggs, fresh fruit platters, and specialty coffees.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Edelweiss in Mürren — a premium mountain restaurant with panoramic Jungfrau massif views. Order the Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce with Rösti) and a glass of Fendant white wine.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience arranged by the resort — a personal chef prepares a bespoke four-course meal in your suite featuring seasonal Swiss Alpine ingredients, paired with a curated wine flight selected by the resort sommelier.

day_by_day.notes: The Schilthorn and Mürren area requires a separate cable car ticket — the resort concierge can bundle this into the ski pass. Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at 2,970m offers one of the most dramatic panoramas in the Alps. Book the private chef in-suite dinner at least 24 hours in advance. Ski school for children should be reserved 48 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Depart at 09:30 for the Ice Skating at Davos — the world's largest natural ice rink at over 18,000 sq meters. The family enjoys a private skating session with a professional ice skating coach. Skate hire is premium quality with heated boot options. The vast open rink with mountain backdrop is truly world-class and a unique family memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skating, explore the charming town of Davos — browse the luxury boutiques and artisan shops on the Promenade. Visit the Kirchner Museum Davos, an architecturally stunning gallery dedicated to expressionist artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, for a cultural interlude. Return to the resort by 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort's panoramic bar — Swiss Spritz, Alpine G&Ts, and non-alcoholic elderflower pressés for the family. Followed by a premium farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort — avocado toast, smoked salmon bagels, fresh juices, and specialty coffees for an active morning ahead.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Bolgenschanze in Davos — an elegant mountain restaurant with terrace views over the Davos valley. Try the pan-seared Arctic char, truffle pasta, and a local Graubünden wine.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's signature fine dining room — seven-course Alpine Haute Cuisine tasting menu featuring foie gras, Wagyu beef, black truffle risotto, and a Swiss chocolate and praline dessert experience. Champagne welcome toast with Billecart-Salmon Blanc de Blancs.

day_by_day.notes: Davos is approximately 1.5 hours from the Jungfrau region by car — arrange a private luxury transfer. The natural ice rink is weather-dependent; confirm conditions the evening before. The Kirchner Museum is closed on Mondays, so Saturday is ideal. Book the farewell dinner at the resort well in advance as it is likely to be in high demand during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at the resort. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at your own pace. Take a gentle snowshoe walk through the resort's private Alpine forest trail (guided, 1.5 hours) for a peaceful final morning in the Swiss Alps — a perfect contrast to the high-energy activities of the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for checkout formalities. Enjoy a final spa treatment — a 60-minute Swiss Alpine herbal body wrap or hot stone massage as a farewell wellness ritual. Luggage is handled by the resort's dedicated concierge team. Private luxury transfer departs at 15:00 to the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel. The resort concierge will prepare a luxury travel hamper for the journey — Swiss chocolates (Läderach or Sprüngli), artisan cheeses, and a bottle of Swiss wine as a farewell gift.

meals.breakfast: Extended à la carte farewell breakfast at the resort — eggs any style, Swiss waffles with berry compote, artisan pastries, smoked fish platter, and a full coffee and tea service.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort's terrace café — club sandwiches, Caesar salads, truffle soup, and fresh-pressed Alpine juices.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the departure airport's premium lounge or on the return flight.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort (typically 12:00, but late checkout until 14:00 may be available for premium guests — request in advance). Allow at least 3 hours for the transfer to Zurich or Geneva airport. The resort's concierge can arrange Swiss chocolate and souvenir shopping delivery to your suite the evening before departure. Ensure ski equipment rentals are returned before checkout.
